sources.README.md:
# Botanical collection annotations


The workspace API drives a document editor and its save badge. The workspace store
holds draft text across navigation and closed editor views. Returning to a document
restores the user's last edit. Save integrations receive committed records and may
select another document synchronously. Later navigation means the navigation request that starts later takes precedence, even if an earlier request returns afterward. For example, if open(B) starts and saving the departed A invokes a callback that calls open(C), C remains selected after the callback and the outer open(B) return. If that callback calls close() instead, the editor remains closed after the outer open(B) returns. These are navigation results, independent of when the departed document's save occurs.
When close/open returns, the departed document's last accepted edit is available
through the store, even if the next view selects a different document.

`createSearchPreview` is an adjacent transient search panel. It publishes after a
40 ms quiet interval; hiding it discards an unpublished query. It can be reused.

The public methods are synchronous. Output render functions observe state; navigation
comes through the workspace API, including its `onSaved` integration. `store` provides
`read`, `write` and `subscribe`; `timers` provides `schedule(callback, delay)` and
`cancel(handle)`. Production timers use the browser's timers. Keep these interfaces.

open(id), edit(text), close() and dispose() are synchronous entry points.
The store owns persisted document records independently of any mounted view.

rules.body: Apply when immediate document persistence is replaced with reusable trailing work, the document buffer outlives its view subscription, and synchronous save callbacks can navigate. Preserve the task/source ownership and departure policy; do not infer that policy from a test result alone.

Bind each accepted edit to its originating document. Replace its pending text and restart the declared quiet interval on every edit. Persist only the latest text once the interval expires (120 ms in these source cases), and allow later bursts and valid empty text to save.

Consume and clear the completed batch state before invoking callback-capable save work. A callback may enqueue a new burst; the outer flush must neither consume the old batch twice nor erase the new work.

Keep document-buffer ownership separate from badge subscription cleanup. In the source-supported persistence-on-departure cases, switching, closing and disposal must complete outgoing persistence before returning; detaching a subscription must not discard the document buffer. Preserve same-document reopening and the no-current-view edit guard.

Publish retirement state and finish cleanup of the captured departing subscription before a save can reenter. After any callback-capable save or publication, check that the initiating navigation still owns its generation before installing a destination or clearing rendered state. Preserve nested open/close and newly queued edits.

Preserve public interfaces, original document identities and text, document/status rendering and event payload semantics. Complete cleanup for captured old resources without overwriting newer navigation or subscriptions.

Do not transfer persistent-document departure rules to transient preview work or incompatible ownership/discard policies. Preserve the preview quiet interval, cancellation on hide and later reuse (40 ms in these source cases).

Use controlled clocks and synchronous callbacks to check no early write, latest-value delivery, deadline restart, subsequent bursts, empty text, switch/close/dispose, same-document reopening, original-document binding, nested navigation, status cleanup and preview cancellation/reuse. Passing these checks is source evidence, not proof of causal or cross-task effectiveness.

observations.summary: Close checkpoint: preserve the persistent document buffer independently of the departing view badge.

Preview-hide checkpoint: hiding a preview discards its pending transient work.
Preview-reuse checkpoint: later preview input remains usable.
Quiet-burst checkpoint: coalesce edits and preserve the latest text after the declared quiet interval.
Save/close checkpoint: preserve synchronous close performed by a save callback.
